- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply upward (e.g., > +1.5) followed by a drop, model underreacts — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 2–3% to forecast for first 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (±1.0–1.5) over 3+ consecutive days, model exhibits mean reversion bias — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- If model forecast is >10% above true value for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, sentiment decay (e.g., -0.5–-1.0 per day) should be factored into forecast decay — apply exponential decay with decay factor 0.95–0.98.
